CLARIF ICATION OF DUTIES - DEPUTY GRAND MASTER
AND ASSISTANT GRAND TREASU RER
(89-18)
Should Carry-over Resolution No. 88-15 be adopted, the proponent s of this
Resolution seek to clarify the authority of th.e Assistant Gr~nd !reasurer lo <;tCl
for the Grand Treasurer in the event of his absence or mability to act, with
respect to the withdrawal of Grand Lodge funds.
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A .M. of Califomia:

WHEREA S, Carry-over Resolution No. 88-15, if adopted, w.ould provi~e
for the Assistant Grand Treasurer lo act for the Grand Treasurer w the latter s
absence or inability; and
WHEREA S, Carry-over Resolution No. 88-15, if adopted, will not be
consistent with California Masonic Code Section 1102-lst in that other Grand
Lodge officers are now designated to act for the Grand Treasurer should he be
absent or unable to act with respect to withdrawal of funds of the Grand Lodge
on deposit; and
WHEREA S, the designation of the I?eputy Grand Master in the P.r esent
Section 1102-lst as an alternate under all clfcumstances to act together with the
Grand Secretary to withdraw such funds, should the Grand Tre~surer be abs~nt
or unable is in conflict with California Masonic Code Section 1098 which
provides that the Deputy Grand Master shall only p~rfo~~ the functions of the
Grand Master in the case of the latter's absence or mability to act.

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFOR NIA

283

NOW, THEREFO RE, BE IT RESOLVE D that if Carry-over Resolution
88-15 is adopted, California Masonic Code Section 1102-lst be amended to read
as follows:
To receive all monies belongin~ lo Grand Lodge from the Grand
Secretary, receipt therefor, and immediately upon the receipt of said
monies, to deposit the same to the credit of Grand Lodge, in a bank or
banks selected by the Grand Treasurer with the approval of the Grand
Master. Funds on deposit shall he withdrawn by the Grand Treasurer,.. or in case of his inability or ttftlhttttttbit tt) absence by the Assistant
Grand Treasurer. or in the case of the inability or absence of the
Assistant Grand Treasurer. by the Grand Master or Depttl) Grttnd
Master and the Grand Secretary. acting together.
Respectfully submitted,
Ralph H. Head, PM No. 352
Robert A. Klinger, PM No. 120
The Committee on Jurisprudence:

Your Committee on Jurisprude nce, to which Resolution No. 89-18 has been
referred, reports as follows:
Should carry-over Resolution No. 88-15 be adopted, the proponent s of this
Resolution seek to clarify the authority of the Assistant Grand Treasurer lo act
for the Grand Treasurer in the event of his absence or inability to act, with
respect to the withdrawal of Grand Lodge funds.
Your Committee finds that the legislation as distributed by the Grand
Secretary to the Constituent Lodges is adequate to carry out the intent of the
proponent s.
•
This Resolution seeks to amend the Ordinances and a five-sixths affirmative
vote is required for adoption.
To place the matter before the Grand Lodge, we move the adoption of the
Resolution.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:

Should carry-over Resolution No. 88-15 be adopted, the proponents of this
Resolution seek to clarify the authority of the Assistant Grand Treasurer to act
for the Grand Treasurer in the event of bis absence or inability to act, with
respect to the withdrawal of Grand Lodge funds.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes agrees that carry-over
Resolution No. 88-15 does not address sufficient detail with respect to specific
duties and that if adopted, Section 1102-lst would require modification to
accomplish the full intent of the proponents.
Therefore, your Committee on Policy and General Purposes recommends
a "Yes" vote on this "housekeeping" Resolution.
Resolution ADOPTED .

GRAND MASTER'S RECOM MENDA TIONS •
TIME LIMIT FOR SUBMIS SION
(89-19)
The proponent of this Resolution seeks to require. the Recommen d!ltions
(but not Decisions) of the Grand Master to be submitted to the constituen t
Lodges sixty days prior to the Annual Communic ation.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:
WHEREA S, it has been recognized that the constituen t Lodges must be
provided ample time to study the Resolution s to be considered at the Annual
Communic allon; and
WHEREA S, the California Masonic Code prescribes specific time ~ts
for the presentatio n, process~ng b~ the. Grand Secretary, review by the CC?mllllttee on Jurisprude nce, and d1sscmmat ion to the Lodge of those Resolution s to
be presented at the Annual Communic ation; and
WHEREA S, the only Decisions and Recommen dations of the Grand
Master which are suhject to those time limits are those which were made as of
the time specified in California Masonic Code Sections 160, 500, 1108-16th, 1204
and 4000; and
WHEREA S, the first notice the Lodges usually receive of the Grand
Master's Recommen dations is during his Message at the Annual Communic ation; and
WHEREA S, the ballot upon a Grand Master's Recommen dation is often
taken on the same day as his Message, thus depriving the constituen t Lodges of
sufficient time to review and understand the Recommen dation, which can result
in misguided or erroneous votes being cast; and
WHEREA S, a Recommen dation by the Grand Master can affect our law
just as significantly as a .Resolution.
NOW, THEREFO RE, BE IT RESOLYEO that the first paragraph of
Section 160 of the California Masonic Code be amended to read as follows:
The transaction of business in Grand Lodge at its Annual Communic ation shall be upon written R esolutions and reports. All such Resolutions must be presented to the Grand Secretary at least 180 days prior
to the commence ment date of the next Annual Commumcation~
~rovided, however, that this restriction shall not apply to Decisionsf lftd
ReeeHHBeRtieloie&s of the Grand Master which are included in his
written Messa~e presented at the Annual C_ommunication, ~
Recommen dations of the Grand Master submitted to the constituen t
Lod2es at least 60 days prior to the Annual Communic ation. nor shall
it applv to emergent matters which may be presented and considered
at any 'time upon consent of five-sixths vote of the members present.>,

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

Our Homes for the children and the elderly are operated solely on the
contributions of Masons, and derive no support from any G overnment Agency
or outside Charity. Since the interest from the Endowment Fund provides nearly
half of the financial support needed to operate the Ho mes, it is vital that those
contribuLions be received by Grand Lodge at the earliest possible time. FUither,
those Lodges that hold Funds for a long period of time may jeopardize a
Brother's tax deduction.
Your Committee on Policy and General Purposes feels that sixty days is
ample time for Lodges to transfer those contributions to Grand Lodge and,
therefore, recommends a "Yes" vote.
Resolution HELD OVER.

The Committee on Jurisprndence:

Your Committee on Jurisprudence, to which Resolution No. 89-21 has been
referred, reports as follows:
The proponent of this Resolution see~ to am~nd Section .1602 of the
California Masonic Code so as to have consistency with the appointment and
powers of the Trustees of the Masonic Homes of California and California
Masonic Memorial Temple.
Your Committee finds that the legislation as distributed by the Grand
Secretary to the Constituent Lodges is adequate to carry out the intent of the
proponent.

291

To place the matter before the Grand Lodge, we move the adoption of the
Resolution.
The Committee on Policy and General Purposes:

The proponent of this Resolution seeks to amend Section 2602 of the
California Masonic Code, so the provisions of governin~ the appointment and
removal of Trustees of the Masonic Homes of California, the California
Masonic Temple, and the California Masonic Foundation will be uniform.
Our present law provides as to Trustees of Masonic Homes of California
and the California Masonic Memorial Temple that a Trustee may be removed
by the Grand Master only when two-thirds of the Trustees so r~uest. This
Resolution would apply the same standard to the Foundation Boarcl.
We believe the change is warranted and may even by required.
First: The Masonic Homes of California, the California Masonic Memorial
Temple, and the California Masonic Foundation are and each of them is a
corporation organized under the laws of the State of California.
Each is classified as a 501(c)(3) corporation under the Internal Revenue
Code of the United States, and each has tax exempt status.
This status encourages our charity by making our donations tax deductible.
We should not end<}Dger that tax exempt status.
To allow the Grand Master to change the composition of the Trustees at
his will subjects us to challenge by the Internal Revenue Service because of
"one-man control".
Second: Though we support, without reservation, the Grand Master' s
autonomy, in this single area we believe it must yield to legitimate government
concern.
To create the uniformity for such a valid purpose is appropriate.
We recommend a "Yes" vote.
Resolution HELD OVER.

No evidence has been presented to this Commi~tee that ~y .Masonic
Temple Association has placed its Non-Profit Corporation. Charter m Jeopardy
by adopting the uniform set of By-Laws mandated by Section 2305.

The Committee on Temple Properties:
Although we. agree with ~he intent of t.his Re~olution, we feel th~t the
California Masoruc Code Section 2305 permits the mtent to be accomplished
already.
Therefore, we recommend a "No" vote on Resolution No. 89-23.

The Committee on Taxation:
This Resolution seeks to avoid the present requirement that Masonic
Temple Corporations adopt the Uniform By-Laws prescribed by the California
Masonic Code.
The Uniform By-Laws were developed by the Grand Lodge for the purpose
of demonstrating adherence to the rules for exempt organizations.
The Taxation Committee believes there is benefit to California Masonic
Temple Corporations that by adoption of the Uniform By-Laws make positive
their intent to adhere to rules for exempt from taxation status.
The proponents of the Resolution do not identify any benefit to be obtained
by adoption of Resolution No. 89-23.
The Taxation Committee recommends a "No" vote.

ALTERNATIVE LIFE MEMBERSHIP PLAN

BE IT RESOLVED that the California Masonic Code be amended by
adding Section 2805, to read as follows:

(89-27)

2805. ALTERNATE LIFE MEMBERSHIP PLAN

The proponents of this Resolution se~k t'! have the incoming ~rand Mast~r
appoint a Special Committee to draft legislatton to carry out the mtent of theu
proposed Alternative Life Membership Plan.

I. A Lodge may, by Standing Resolution, adopt the Alternate Life

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of Califomill:

2. Said Resolution shall become effective only after approval of the
Grand Master, and shall be granted to any member in good standing,
upon the/ayment of a sum equal to the annual dues of his Lodge
multiplie by the Life Membership factor indicated opposite the
member's age in the following schedule.

'

WHEREAS, a system of Life Membership is currently authorized m
Section 2804 of the California Masonic Code; and
WHEREAS, the present system requires a minimum of $250.00 to become
a Life Member, and applies only to the Lodge of record; and
WHEREAS flexible Life Membership Plans which provide for the transfer
of memberships ~d the mergin~ of Life Membership Funds for investment
purposes have proven successful rn yielding a higher investment rate of return
because of consolidation of funds under central management; and
WHEREAS, a Life Membership Plan based on the ~ember's age and his
annual dues is more effective, realistic and more responsive to the needs of a
Master Mason; and
WHEREAS, a member may not be able to afford to pay for Life Membership in a lump sum; and
WHEREAS, it is now impossible to purchase a Life Membership as a
Memoriam.
NOW THEREFORE BE IT RESOLVED that the incoming Grand
Master be 'directed to appoint a Special Committee for the purpose of ~raft~g
appropriate legislation to carry ~mt ~he intent of the. proposed. Alternative Life
Membership Plan, a copy of which 1s attached to this Resolutton.
Respectfully submitted,
Cecil W. Crowe, PM No. 356
Donald Herwg, PM No.126
Clarence H. Wikse, PM No. 30
K.O. Guyer, PM No. 126
Edward D. Doss, PM No. 57
Clyde Anderson, PM No. 181
R.W. Boltz, PM No. 126

3. A Lodge may collect partial payments by members for Life Membership. Said monies to be retained by the Lodge in a specified account
until the member has accrued the entire amount which will then be
transferred immediately to the Grand Secretary's office and such funds
will be placed in the Life Membership Fund, and credited to the proper
Lodge.
3A. The member must continue to pay the annual
dues in effect until the entire amount for Life Membership has been paid.

3B. All partial payments are non-refundable and
non-transferable.
3C. Upon the death, dimit or withdrawal from his

Lodge and from the Grand Lodge of California, or
loss of membership by suspension, expulsion or exclusion, the Life Membership deposit shall immediately be forwarded to the Life Membership Fund.
The amount being credited to the proper Lodge
account.
3D. If at the time of death, a member has accrued a
sum ~eater than $100.00 in ,eartial payment towards
his Life Membership, his Ltfe Membership shall be
considered paid in full and so issued.
3E. All interest received from partial payment of Life
Memberships being held by a member's Lodge shall
go into that individual Lodge general fund not less
than annually.

COMMITTEE REPORTS
The following Grand Lodge Committees and Board, at the request of the
Grand Master, did not present an oral report during the various sessions of the
Annual Communication. They did, however, present their reports in writing and
are herewith included in these proceedings.

To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.&A.M. of California:

In response to this request, it was necessary for your Committ.ee on Policy
and General Purposes to research the ~tory of t~e. Order of Kni~ht Mas~ms
to determine its origin, as well as to establish its validity as a Masor:ic ?rgaruzation. We have, th.rough our efforts, determined that the Order is, mdeed, a
recognized Order of Masons.

In the interest of time we have elected not to burden this report with detail
as to qualifying informati~n. It should be pointed o~t, ~owever, t~at membership can only be attained by a member in good standing m a Conslltuent Lodge
who also is in good standing as a Royal Arch Mason. We do have records that
trace the Order back to the seventeen hundreds.
At the present time there 3!e approximately l<>p ~ asons residing in California who are members of Knight Mason Councils m Colorado, Nevada or
Arizona. It is our opinion that California Masonry .w<?uld b~st b.e served by
permitting these Brothers to exercise that membership 10 Califorrua, and thus,
meet and adhere to a California agenda.
We concur with the conditions of the Resolution, t~a~ n? more t~an ~o
Councils of Knight Masons would be warranted in the J unsd1chon of Califorrua.
As a matter of General policy, it has been a con<7rn. of this Committe.c that
it is possible that the great number of Orders, Orgaruzat10n~ and Clubs, appendant to this Grand Lodge, may indeed, serve to the detnment of our Craft
Lodges. We need not re~terate the ~emands pl~ced upon our most capable
Masons due to their mulllple Masomc memberships.

We make exception to our concern, in this instance, and recommend a "Yes"
vote.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON
CALIFORNIA FREEMASON PUBLICATION
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:

A Board consisting of the Grand Master, Grand Secretary, such Advisors
as may be desirable, and an Editor-in-Chief, appointed by the Grand Master,
administer the quarterly editing and distribution of the California Freemason,
an official publication of the Grand Lodge.
The magazine is now in its 36th year. More than 20,500,000 copies have
been distributed to members of California Lodges, other Grand Junsdictions
and to paid subscribers since its founding.
The goal of the Publication Committee is to keep Califomia Masons
informed as to the activities of Grand Lodge, the Masonic Homes, the California Masonic Foundation, the California Memorial Temple and particularly, of
the Lodges of this Jurisdiction.
Activities repprted during the past year have been Cornerstone
Ceremonies, Constitutional Observances, Public Schools Week activities.
During the year, hundreds of news items appeared in the magazine about
Golden Veterans' Awards, Hiram Awards, Laymen's and Widow's Nights.
For $2.00, California Masons may buy a two-year gift subscription to the
California Freemason for relatives and friends. There may be no better way to
spread the good news about Freemasonry to the general public.
Respectfully submitted,

Application APPROVED.

Ralph H. Head, Editor
Stanley L. Channon

Robert A. Klinger

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON
COLUMBIA MASONIC TEMPLE
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:

Fourteen Lodges and affiliated groups visited the Columbia Masonic
Temple this year.
The Columbia Masonic Temple is part of the Columbia State Park. The
Park is unique, no entrance fee or parking fees are charged.
All the debris remaining in the basement from the flood of February 1986
has been removed and hauled away.
New floors have been installed in the two Museum viewing areas.
We have a new Custodian this year and his conscientious efforts are
appreciated.
Respectfully submitted,

Lewis R. Morris, Chairman
Herbert G. Waltz

Robert S. Rathbone
George R. Eaton

Referred to Committee on Finance (Budget Allocation).

In preparation for publishing a history book of all the Lodges in California,
the CoDlDllttee has been gathering Lodge histories and condensing and editing
them for publication.
The history book will include histories of Lodges which have merged with
other Lodges or surrendered their charter~ - some 840 Lo.dg~s. We expect to
include pictures of Lodge Temples - espeetally the old buildmgs - so that the
eventual publication will be a premier source of California Lodge history.

ANNUAL REPORT OF THE
MASONIC HOMES ENDOWMENT BOARD
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A .M. of California:
Your Masonic Homes Endowment Board is pleased to submit its 57th
Annual Report covering the fiscal year e nding June 30 1989. Tl;tro ugh the
Commitment and
enthusiasm and dedication of the Board members, and
support of the Brethren of this great Fraternity to the Residents '?f .our two
Homes, contributions to the Endowment Fund were over one million four
hundred thousand dollars.

the

INCOME FROM THE PERMANENT ENDOWMENT FUND
Income from the Masonic Homes Endowment Fund amounted to
$5,799,899.25 which was transferred to the operat~g accoll;Dts of the Maso~c
Homes of California. This income is an extremely vital and unportant fac.tor ~
providing the Homes' Trustees with a portion of the funds ?ecessary to mamtam
the exceptionally hish 9uality of ~~alth care and services afforded to the
Residents and to assist m the providing for the present, as well as the future,
construction and enhancement of the facilities at both our Homes.

We are pleased to report that the average contribution per contributor
increased by $0.39 to $18.75 while the percent of members contributing increased almost a half of one percent to 49.22%. The first year of the new Honor
Roll requirements based on the average gift of the membership of the prior year
is now history and it is heartening to see that not only did the average contribution per contributor increase but so did the percent of the members participating.
Obviously the number of Lodges that attained Honor Roll status did
decline as expected because it is now more difficult to achieve; however, the
reduction was in line with that which was expected.
The overall average gift of the membership increased to $9.27 per member
(including Hawaii) even though the membership declined by 5,824 members.
Now that Hawaii has•formed its own Grand Lodge, we have lost an additional
2,692 members for a total loss of 8,516 members last year. It now becomes even
more important to reach the more than 50% of our members who do not
contribute to the Homes Endowment Fund.
In calculating the requirements for the Honor Roll for fiscal year ending
June 30, 1990, it was jud$,ed to be fair to deduct contributions made by members
of the Lodges of Hawaii and their membership from the 1989 totals. For the
Endowment Year of 1990, a Lodge will be eligible to receive Honor R oll status
when it achieves an average contribution of $9.27 per member.
The total contributions to the Endowment Fund is made up of the contributions from members through their Lodges and from Bequests, Gifts and
Memorials. This latter category of contribution is at the lowest level in more
than ten years and its nature is very unpredictable.
Many factors effect the Bequests, Gifts and Memorials contributions such
as other Grand Lodge Projects that are competing for our members discretionary dollars. A vivid presentation of how this category of giving has declined is
shown in the graph entitled Endowment Fund - Total Contributions at the end
of this report.

Annual Communication by a member of the Endowment Board. For Lodges
which have achieved H onor Roll status for the first time, certificates and tabs
will be presented in a like manner.

PROCEEDINGS OF THE

GRAND LODGE OF CALIFORNIA

EPILOGUE

REPORT OF CONTRIBUTIONS TO ENDOWMENT FUND

Our sincere and grateful thanks to Grand Master Stanley L. Channon and
to the Grand Lodge Officers, Board members, and Committeemen, all of whom
have been most supportive of the Endowment Program. We also wish to thank
the Masters, Wardens and Secretaries of the Lodges for their efforts in furthering this worthy program.
We also extend a special thanks to the 75,762 Brothers who through their
continued generosity, contributed almost one and a half million dollars to the
Endowment Fund during this past year.
We appreciate the splendid assistance and support we have received from
the Homes Board of Trustees, the Grand Secretary's office under the leadership
of Grand Secretary Robert A. Klinger and the staff in the Grand Lodge office.
My personal thanks to every Homes Endowment Board member for their
dedication and devotion in the support extended to me during this year as your
Chairman. No other group of people can measure up to the contribution given
by the members the Endowment Board. Many new demands were placed upon
them with the initiation of new programs and it is gratifying that the response
was magnificent. My hat is off to the members of tlie Endowment Board.
Respectfully submitted,
John M. Palmer, Chairman

REPORT OF COMMITTE E ON
MASONIC WIDOWS
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:

The objectives of the Masonic Widows Program is to let the wives of our
departed Brothers know that they have not been forgotten, and that we care
about them.

All Brothers, when contacted to work on the Masonic Widows Committee,
are asked to serve at least three years if appointed by the Grand Master . We
feel that it takes one year to know the demands of the Lodges and how the
Committeemen can fulfill those demands.
The members of the Masonic Widows Committee arc dedicated to provide
the help needed for every Masonic Lodge in California to have a successful
Widows Program.
All the members of the Committee have from three to ten volunteers
helping to keep the program before the Lodges. This has been very successful,
for now over ninety percent of the Lodges participate in the program.
The Masonic Widows Committee has four meetings each year, two in the
South and two in the North. We have invited other Grand Lodge Committees
to join us at our meetings so we may broaden our scope of knowledge on how
to help each other in promoting Masonry in California. We believe this to be a
good practice for all the Grand Lodge Committees.
The Widow's Pins and Certificates are in great demand from the Lodges
along with the family survivors booklets.

$9.23

. . • . . . . . . • . . . • . . . • . . . . . . . . . . . . . . . $9.23
OVERALL AVERAGE GIFT .
A VERAGE CONTRIBUTION P E R COl'ITRIBlffOR . . . . . . . • . • . . . · · · · · · $18.75

The Widows Committee bas included in our presentations to the Lod~es
the information on the Masonic Homes and we encourage the Lodges to visit
both of the Homes.
Credit for the success of this Committee belongs to the members and their
dedication to the Widows Program.
Respectfully submitted,

Arizona Masonry
The Grand Lodge has purchased the video tape "An Evening with Judge
Sentelle". In this Video, Judge David Sentelle discusses his encounter with the
U.S. Senate Judiciary Committee while being conformed for appointment as a
Judge on the U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals. This Committee was going to reject
his appointment solely on the fact that he is a Mason until several Masonic
Brothers who a.re influencial Senators and Congressme n appeared before the
Committee and testified on his behalf. Senator Strom Thurmond was one of his
strong supporters during the hearings. Their testimony resulted in his confirmation for appointment as a Judge.
King Solomon Lodge No. 5 had an "open house" during the three
Helldorado days in Tombstone. The Lodge room being opened to the general
public was reported well received and appreciated by the visitors. The open
house was a response to the 1unior Past Grand Master's thought of "Freemasonry is Good, let's talk about it".

'

The Grand Master gave Recommend ations to be presented at the Annual
Communicat ions that would allow a Lodge to go dark for two months; reduce
age to nineteen to petitioner; allow Lodge Secretaries to vote at Grand Lodge.

The North Dakota Mason
Lemhi Lodge No. 11, Salmon, Idaho is one of the few remaining "Moon"
Lodges le ft in the U oited States. The custom originated because members could
see to ride their horses, donkeys, etc. from their ranches and mines to the Lodge
by the light of the moon. The Lodge celebrated its lOOth birthday in 1974.

Grand Lodge of India
Presently, the Grand Master is elected for a term of three years and can be
re-elected for one further term of three years. It was proposed that this be
changed so that the Grand Master could be elected for only one three year term.
In the past twenty-five years, the number of Lodges bas almost doubled and
membership bas increased about 35%. The Board of General Purposes
reported that in 1985, one Lodge of258 failed to file the annual report and pay
Grand Lodge dues. ln 1987, 31 Lodges out of 272 failed to file. The financial
position of the Grand Lodge is considered satisfactory.

Missouri Freemason
At the Grand Lodge Communicat ion, the most far reaching legislation was
the revision of the Grand Lodge By-Laws covering solicitation of Candidates.
The section in question is, "It is a Masonic offense to im{>roperly solicit petitions
of Candidates for degrees". "Improper solicitation" bemg defmed as any form
of coercion. Because of the vague wording of the section, the Grand Lodge must
try to provide guidelines to prevent any improper solicitation.

Iowa Grand Lodge BuJJetin
The Grand Master stated that he is a hard-nose ritualist, but now encourages reducing the. amout of rote memory required for advancemen t from
one degree to the next in view of the high number of members failing to advance
to the next degree, hence, being dropped from Masonry.

REPORT OF COMMITTEE ON
TAXATION
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:

The Taxation Committee is pleased to report its activities for the Masonic
year ended September, 1989:
Resolutions for the 1989 Annual Communication were referred to the
Committee for its report. The Committee has responded with its report on 89-23
and 88-19.
The Committee bas received about twelve telephone requests for advice on
tax matters. All of the requests were resolved during the first phone call. Most
inquiries were the question, "Do we have to file?" forms 990 and 199.
O_ne le~t er was received complainin~ a~out paying $?<).00 for prep~ration
of CaJ1forrua Form 199 - Exempt Orgaruzallon - and paymg a $10.00 fihng fee
to the Franchise Tax Board. No answer was provided because the cost of
pre paring the forms and the filing fee are too small to be out-of-line.
The Committee prepared a memo "To all Lodges and Hall Associations"
outlining important filing requirements for Organizations Exempt from Income
Tax. The memo with a copy of Forms 990 and 199 and instructions went forward
to each Lodge Secretary of all Lodges in California through the Grand
Secretary's Office in San Francisco.
R espectfully submitted,
Charles B. Morgan, Chainnan

TRAVEL ALLOWANCES
To the Most Worshipful Grand Lodge, F.& A.M. of California:

The Committee on Travel Allowances submits the following report covering the 140th Annual Communication of Grand Lodge.
Those entitled to travel allowances are the Master, or in his absence, the
ranking Warden, or in the absence of the Master and Wardens, the duly elected
Representative in accordance with Section 1148 of the California Masonic
Code. However, no payment shall be alJowed for the Officers or Representatives of any Lodge, the dues of which have not been paid in full, or which
shall be reported by the Grand Secretary as having been delinquent in the
transmission of Certificates of the E lection and Installation of Officers of their
respective Lodges.
Past Grand Masters, not on Committees, will be reimbursed as provided in
Section 1150 of the California Masonic Code.
In accordance with Section 1148 of the California Masonic Code, when a
Master and Warden from the same Lodge arc present at a Communication, and
one of said Officers serves on a Grand Lode Committee entitled to travel and
expense reimbursement, he shall be reimbursed under Section 1150 of the
California Masonic Code. The other Officer shall receive reimbursement under
Section 1148 of the California Masonic Code, as the Officer representing his
Lodge on the noor of Grand Lodge.
Mileage from the various points within the State of California to San
Francisco has been taken from the published records of the California State
Automobile Association in accordance with Section 1148 of the California
Masonic Code. No compensation is allowed to members representing Lodges
in San Francisco and the immediate 30 mile vicinity. Compensation to members
from the State of California has been computed on the basis of eleven (11) cents
per mile, the rate fixed by the Committee on Finance.
Checks will be ready for distribution at the Registration Desk on "G" Floor
immediately following the Election of the Junior Grand Warden in accordance
and as noted in the program for the 140th Annual Communication. Brethren,
if you are the Master or Warden representing your Lodge, or the duly elected
Representative of your Lodge, the Committee on Travel Allowances urgently
requests you to pick up your check. You must present a properly validated
credential. Arrangements have been made so that those who may wish to cash
their checks can do so at the Fairmont H otel Branch of the First Interstate Bank
located at California and Mason Streets. The entrance is on California Street.
Your Grand Lodge credential will serve as suitable identification. Checks not
picked up will be mailed to the Lodges.

The member of the Travel Allowances Committee wish to express their
sincere appreciation to members of the Grand Lodge office staff for their
cooperation throughout the year in assembling, preparing and computing the
detail necessary for the functioning of this Committee.

We have audited the accompanying balance sheets of the California Hasonic
Foundation, a California nonprofit corporation, at June 30, 1989 and 1988, and the
related statements -0f support, revenue and expenses and changes in fund balances
for the years then ended. These financial statements are the responsibility of
the Foundation's management. Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these
financial statements based on our audit.
We conducted our audit in accordance with generally accepted auditing
standards. Those standards require that "e plan and perform the audit to obtain
reasonable assurance about whether the financial statements are free of material
misstatement. An audit includes examining, on a test basis, evidence supporting
the amounts and disclosures in the financial statements. An audit also includes
assessing the accounting principles used and significant estimates made by
management, as l'ell as evaluating the overall financial statement presentation.
We believe that our audit provides a reasonable basis for our opinion.
In our opinion, the financial statements referred to above present fairly, in
all material respects, the financial position of the California Hasonic Foundation
at June 30, 1989 and 1988 and the results of its operations and changes in fund
balances for the years then ended in conformity l'ith generally accepted accounting
principles.
Our audit l'as made for the purpose of forming an opinion on the bas ic
financial statements taken as a whole.
The graphically displayed financial
information appearing in Exhibits C and 0 ls presented for the purposes of
additional analys is and ls not a required part of the bas lc financial statements .
Such information has been subjected to the auditing procedures applied in the
audit of the bas ic financial statement s and, in our opinion, is fairly stated in
all materi al respects in relation to the basi c financial s tatements taken as a
whole.
